name: update_serial_handshake_state
description: Copies a status byte into the serial state record and sets a pending bit, then either sets a shared status word when a control bit is clear or clears the pending byte. It touches the CIA port and interrupt enable registers as part of the handshake.

name: clear_serial_pending_byte
description: Clears one pending-status byte in the serial unit's state record and returns. It has no other effect.

name: begin_serial_read_request
description: Marks a request as active when its flag is not yet set, zeroes a counter, loads a length from the caller's buffer minus ten, and makes a library call. It sets a status byte when the returned value is nonzero.

name: service_pending_request_flag
description: Clears a request-active bit and, if it was set and the shared status word has no low-bit activity, sets a follow-up flag and calls a handler through the device table. A saved pointer is copied into the request record first when it is empty.

name: receive_serial_character_into_buffer
description: Reads a masked data word and either compares it against two stored characters to set a status flag, or stores the character into a ring buffer. The write pointer wraps at the buffer limit and the received count is incremented.

name: flag_serial_ready_and_notify
description: Sets a ready bit in the request record, copies the current buffer pointer if none is stored, and calls a device handler through the table. It is the simpler form of the request-ready notifier.

name: queue_or_activate_serial_request
description: Clears the completion counter and, when a pending flag is set and no requests are queued, either activates the request or places it on a list. Once handled, it calls a device handler unless a status bit already covers the case.

name: activate_pending_serial_request
description: Activates a request by storing it as the current request and setting the shared status word to a fixed value, when the request's error byte is not set. Otherwise it sets a status bit and returns.

name: stub_return_only
description: A routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It performs no work.

name: set_status_byte_on_flags
description: Tests two bit groups of the shared status word and, when both are set, stores the value thirteen into a status byte of the record passed in. Otherwise it leaves the record unchanged.

name: advance_serial_transmit_state
description: Advances the transmit state: it hands out the next queued request from a list, or reads the next byte from the active buffer and checks it against a status mask. It updates the transmit counters and the shared status word, and completes the request through a library handler when the count is reached.

name: transmit_next_serial_byte
description: Resets a retry count and reads the next byte from the active buffer, posting a masked status word when the count is within its limit. It advances the buffer and count pointers and completes the request through a handler when finished.

name: resume_serial_transmit_step
description: Resumes the transmit step only when the counter has reached the given limit, and otherwise returns early. When it proceeds it posts a masked status word, advances the pointers and counts, and finishes the request through a library handler.

name: record_serial_completion_status
description: Combines a status word from a library call with the stored status bits and writes the result to the shared status word. It advances the buffer and count pointers and, if the count passes the limit, stores the count and completes the request through a library handler.

name: dequeue_next_serial_request
description: When the request list count is nonzero, it removes the first request from the list, decrements the count, resets the counters and stores the buffer pointer. It calls a further handler when the request type is ten, and otherwise sets the shared status word to one.

name: set_serial_status_idle
description: Sets the shared status word to one and returns, with no other work.

name: post_serial_pending_status
description: Clears a pending byte in the request record and loads the shared status word from a saved status value combined with that byte. It sets the status word to one when neither queue has entries.

name: initialize_serial_unit_defaults
description: Resets the pending state and clears the request lists, then loads default configuration values into the unit record. It finishes by setting the shared status word and calling a library handler when a flag is clear.

name: notify_serial_request_completion
description: Calls an unnamed routine that deals with the record, then calls a library handler when the record's status bits are all clear. It is the completion notifier for a finished request.

name: query_and_notify_serial_state
description: Marks the request as pending when its list pointer is set, then calls an unnamed routine when a second list is non-empty. It notifies through a library handler when the record's status bits are clear and returns the unnamed routine's result.

name: finish_pending_serial_request
description: Clears a pending bit in the request record and, when a second record is attached, calls an unnamed routine on it. It sets the shared status word to a fixed value and calls a library handler when the record's status bits are clear.

name: cycle_serial_state_and_notify
description: Sets the shared status word to one value, calls an unnamed routine, then sets it to another value. It notifies through a library handler when the record's status bits are clear.

name: drain_serial_request_list
description: Walks a linked list of requests, unlinking each entry from the head and passing it to an unnamed routine until the list is empty.

name: stub_return_only
description: A routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It performs no work.

name: capture_serial_line_status
description: Reads a line status byte from a hardware port, masks it, and adds a bit when two control flags are set. It stores the result and the current count into the request record, clears two bits of a control flag, and calls a handler when the record is idle.

name: route_serial_request_to_queue
description: Clears a status bit on the record and, when a request is already active or the queue has entries, appends the record to the queue and increments the queue count. Otherwise it calls an unnamed routine and makes the returned record the current request, writing a hardware control register.

name: start_or_clear_current_request
description: Calls an unnamed routine and either makes the returned record the current request and writes a hardware control register, or notifies a handler and clears the current request pointer.

name: notify_and_clear_current_request
description: Calls a library handler through the device table and then clears the current request pointer. It is the release step for an active request.

name: complete_special_request_and_notify
description: When a flag is set and the request type is ten, it clears the current request, writes a hardware control register and notifies a handler. It then sets the shared status word to a fixed value.

name: start_timed_serial_request
description: Sets the shared status word to one, stores a value and a time-out count into the request record, then calls a library function. It sets a status byte when the returned value is nonzero.

name: update_serial_control_flags
description: Sets or clears a control bit according to a flag on the record, and when no transfer is pending and the queues are empty it calls an unnamed routine. Otherwise it marks the record with a status value of one, then notifies a handler when the record is idle.

name: clear_control_flag_and_check
description: Clears a control bit and, when no transfer is pending and the queues are empty, calls an unnamed routine. Otherwise it sets a status value of one and notifies a handler when the record is idle.

name: run_serial_check_and_notify
description: Sets the shared status word, calls an unnamed routine, then restores it to a second value. It notifies through a library handler when the record's status bits are clear.

name: validate_and_apply_serial_parameters
description: Checks that the requested unit parameters fall within fixed bounds, then copies them and their flags into the device state and calls unnamed routines to apply them. It keeps the timing field only when the configuration is valid.

name: compute_serial_bit_masks
description: Builds a bit mask from the unit's configured bit index, doubling it for one mode and shifting it for another. It stores the mask and the masks derived from two unnamed routine calls into the device state.

name: set_status_code_five
description: Stores the value five into a status byte of the record passed in and returns.

name: compute_serial_timing_divisor
description: Multiplies a stored value by seven and divides a fixed 25 million clock constant by the result, using a shifted path for large values. It stores the 16-bit quotient as the timing divisor and updates the status bits for a special unit type.

name: set_serial_divisor_from_registers
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a 16-bit value and stores the quotient as the timing divisor, updating the shared status word. For a special unit type with a flag set, it also marks the status bits.

name: allocate_serial_device_unit
description: Allocates a serial unit record through a library call and, when that succeeds, initializes its request fields and list heads. It returns one on success and zero when the allocation fails.

name: initialize_serial_request_lists
description: Initializes two request list heads and default fields on the unit record, then sets up a list entry through an unnamed routine. It sets the shared status word to one and returns one.

name: fill_device_request_block
description: Fills in a request block by storing a link to a caller-supplied structure, a fixed byte value of sixteen, a pointer to a shared variable, and two register values into fixed fields.

name: configure_serial_unit_request_block
description: Sets default values on the unit record, initializes two request lists through an unnamed routine, and calls a library function. It sets the shared status word to one and returns one.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any other work.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes here do not decode to a valid routine; the decompiler produced only a halt marker, so no logic is recovered. It is a stub entry with no behaviour.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes here do not decode to a valid routine; the decompiler produced only a halt marker, so no logic is recovered. It is a stub entry with no behaviour.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes here do not decode to a valid routine; the decompiler produced only a halt marker, so no logic is recovered. It is a stub entry with no behaviour.

name: increment_counter_clear_flag
description: Increments a 16-bit counter stored in a library record and clears bit three of a status byte in the same record.

name: decrement_reference_and_cleanup
description: Decrements a 16-bit count in a library record and, when it reaches zero and a flag bit is set, calls a cleanup routine and returns its result. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: remove_library_list_entry
description: When a link field is zero, it calls a library function with a stored value and unlinks the record from its list. Otherwise it sets a pending flag bit and returns zero.

name: set_pending_flag_return_zero
description: Sets a pending flag bit in the record and returns zero.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any other work.

name: open_dos_library_or_alert
description: Stores two pointers in the record and calls a library function that refers to the DOS library. If the call returns nothing it raises an alert; otherwise it saves the two pointers to shared variables.

name: copy_two_pointers_from_record
description: Copies two 32-bit fields from a record addressed by a register into two shared variables and returns.

name: forward_call_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: relay_call_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: delegate_call_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: pass_control_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: wrap_helper_invocation
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: route_call_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: chain_to_helper_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: invoke_helper_and_return
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: hand_off_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: relay_to_helper_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: delegate_to_helper_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: tail_call_helper_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: bridge_to_helper_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: trampoline_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: store_value_in_returned_record
description: Calls a library function through a table to obtain a pointer, then stores the second argument at a fixed offset within the record that pointer refers to.

name: create_record_with_registration
description: Creates a record through an unnamed routine, registers it with a second unnamed routine, and returns it. If the registration fails, it releases the record through a third unnamed routine and returns zero.

name: read_icon_info_into_record
description: Creates a record and reads a block of values into a local buffer through an unnamed routine. It copies the buffer's 44 bytes and several fields into the record, links it to its parent, and returns it; if the read fails it releases the record and returns zero.

name: copy_icon_state_fields
description: Copies 44 bytes from a stack buffer into a record at a fixed offset, along with several 32-bit and byte fields, and links the record to its parent when one is set.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any other work.

name: pack_icon_record_for_send
description: Packs a record into a stack buffer that begins with a fixed two-word header and a version word of one. It copies 44 bytes and several fields into the buffer and passes it to an unnamed routine with the first two arguments.

name: validate_icon_header_and_load
description: Opens a named file through an unnamed routine and reads its header, checking that the magic word and version field match fixed values. When they do it reads the remaining fields into the record, and otherwise it returns zero; the routine refers to the .info file type.

name: parse_icon_file_fields
description: Checks an in-memory header against a fixed magic word and version, then reads a sequence of fields and optional sub-blocks into the record through a function table. It returns one when every read succeeds and zero otherwise.

name: read_icon_value_list
description: Reads two words into the record and then, when a count is set, allocates a block and fills it with 32-bit values while a remaining byte count stays above zero. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: read_icon_long_array
description: Reads 32-bit values into a caller-supplied array while a remaining size counter stays above four, then reads one optional pointer field. It returns one on success and zero when a read fails.

name: call_helper_return_zero
description: Calls one unnamed routine and then returns zero.

name: stub_return_only
description: A routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It performs no work.

name: read_icon_record_from_file
description: Allocates a 260-byte work buffer, then reads a sequence of icon fields and optional sub-blocks through unnamed routines. When the allocation fails it records error code 103 and returns zero.

name: emit_icon_fields_via_callback
description: Writes an icon's fields one value at a time through a callback table, including optional sub-blocks and a list of pointers. It returns one when every step succeeds.

name: emit_icon_sublists_and_tail
description: Calls unnamed routines to size and emit the optional sub-blocks and pointer lists of an icon record, then stores a saved offset back into the record. It returns the final status.

name: emit_pointer_list_entries
description: Walks a null-terminated list of pointers, emitting each entry through a callback and adding its size to a running total. It then emits the optional trailing pointer and returns the status.

name: emit_pointer_list_with_trailer
description: Emits each entry of a null-terminated pointer list through a callback, stopping at the first failure, then emits the optional trailing pointer. It returns the final status.

name: walk_chain_releasing_entries
description: Repeatedly takes the next link from a chain through an unnamed routine and passes each one to a second unnamed routine until the chain ends.

name: stub_return_only
description: A routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It performs no work.

name: forward_call_at_record_offset
description: Forwards to another routine with the same first argument and the second argument advanced by a fixed field offset, then returns.

name: allocate_icon_record_block
description: Allocates a 168-byte cleared block, initializes a sub-field, and calls an unnamed routine to attach it. If the attach fails it frees the block and returns zero; otherwise it returns the block.

name: pass_through_to_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any other work.

name: push_pair_into_table
description: Decrements a 16-bit slot counter, refilling the table through an unnamed routine when it is exhausted, then stores two 32-bit values into the next table entry. It returns one on success and zero when the refill fails.

name: store_pair_and_decrement
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter, stores two 32-bit values into the table entry it indexes, and returns one.

name: create_icon_block_with_pair
description: Allocates a 94-byte cleared block with two sub-fields and attaches it through unnamed routines. It returns the block, or releases it and returns zero when an attach step fails.

name: stub_return_only
description: A routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It performs no work.

name: call_library_then_return_zero
description: Calls a library function through the device table and returns zero, ignoring the result.

name: forward_call_with_second_offset
description: Forwards to another routine with the same first argument and the second argument advanced by a different fixed offset, then returns.

name: find_keyed_value_after_equals
description: Searches a list of strings for an entry that starts with the requested name followed by an equals sign, and returns a pointer to the text after the sign. It returns null when no entry matches.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any other work.

name: find_mismatched_chain_record
description: Walks a chain of records, comparing each one's size against a value from an unnamed routine, and returns one when a matching record fails a further check. It returns zero when the chain ends without such a record.

name: scan_chain_for_size_match
description: Scans a chain of records, comparing each record's size against an expected value, and returns one when a size matches and a further check passes. It returns zero when the chain is exhausted.

name: verify_chain_record_size
description: Walks a chain of records and checks each one's size against an expected value, returning one when a record's size matches and its follow-up check passes. It returns zero when no record qualifies.

name: find_chain_entry_by_size
description: Walks a chain of records looking for one whose size equals the expected value and whose follow-up check passes. It returns one when such a record is found and zero otherwise.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any other work.

name: format_copy_label_with_count
description: Reads an optional decimal count from the start of a name string, looking for the word copy and a matching suffix. It stores the parsed count in the record and returns the record.

name: read_copy_count_field
description: Checks for a three-character marker followed by a decimal count and a four-character tag, then calls two unnamed routines to finish the parsed fields. Both branches end with the same finishing calls.

name: parse_decimal_count_tag
description: Reads decimal digits from a text pointer, then checks for a four-character tag after them. It finishes through two unnamed routines whether or not the tag matches.

name: parse_numeric_tag_suffix
description: Accumulates decimal digits from a text pointer into a count, then checks for a four-character suffix and finishes through two unnamed routines. It is the same parser as the neighbouring routines with a different exit path.

name: convert_ascii_digit
description: Converts a character code to its decimal digit value, returning the digit for codes from zero to nine and minus one for any other code.

name: invoke_library_entry_198
description: Calls a library function through a stored library base, using the entry at offset minus 198, and returns nothing.

name: register_or_release_record
description: Calls an unnamed routine to obtain a record and then a second unnamed routine to register it. If the registration fails it releases the record through a third unnamed routine and returns zero.

name: allocate_block_with_length_ten
description: Allocates a 96-byte cleared block, sets a size field and a length byte of ten, and attaches it through an unnamed routine. It returns whether the allocation succeeded.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing any other work.

name: verify_helper_result_matches
description: Calls an unnamed routine with three arguments and returns its result when it equals the fourth argument; otherwise it returns zero.

name: stub_return_only

name: check_helper_result_exact
description: Calls an unnamed routine with three arguments and returns its result when it equals the fourth argument; otherwise it returns zero.

name: stub_return_only

name: divide_unsigned_32_by_16
description: Divides an unsigned 32-bit value by a divisor, returning the quotient and remainder. Divisors wider than 16 bits use a bit-by-bit shift-and-subtract loop, while narrower ones are divided in two 16-bit steps.

name: shift_subtract_divide_step
description: Runs sixteen shift-and-subtract steps on a 32-bit dividend against a divisor, leaving the quotient and remainder in registers. It is the core loop of the wider division path.

name: multiply_32_by_32_partials
description: Computes a 32-bit product from 16-bit partial products of two register operands. It returns the product together with the second operand with its two halves swapped.

name: invoke_text_formatter
description: Calls a text-formatting library function through the global library base at a fixed negative offset and returns nothing. The called routine is the library's raw formatting entry.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the memory location pointed to by an address register.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the characters in a zero-terminated string and returns the count. It uses a decrementing counter whose complement gives the length.

name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for a given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or null when it is absent.

name: stub_return_zero

name: copy_zero_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination, including the terminating zero byte.

name: append_zero_terminated_string
description: Finds the end of the destination string and copies the source string onto it, including its terminating zero byte.

name: strings_differ_within_count
description: Compares two strings for up to a given number of characters. It returns one at the first difference and zero when they match through the limit or the terminator.

name: stub_return_one
description: Returns one without doing any other work.

name: scan_string_with_limit
description: Walks a string up to a given count, stopping at its terminator. When the terminator is reached it calls an unnamed routine, and it does nothing further if the count runs out first.

name: forward_to_string_helper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, performing no other work of its own.

name: copy_string_padded_to_length
description: Copies a source string into a destination of a given size and pads the rest with zero bytes. It never writes past the destination size.

name: stub_return_only

name: init_list_head_block
description: Initializes a list head in a block: the first word points to the next slot, the second word is cleared, and the third word points back to the block.

name: process_icon_block_entry
description: Returns one for a null block. Otherwise it calls an unnamed routine with a fixed size, then calls two further unnamed routines and passes a field of the block to a third; the result is the status of the last call, or zero when the first unnamed routine fails.

name: walk_entries_with_callbacks
description: Walks a linked chain of entries, calling an unnamed routine on each entry's header and on its nested data. It returns one when the chain ends and zero as soon as either unnamed routine fails.

name: stub_return_one

name: stub_return_zero

name: create_icon_block_with_handle
description: When its flag is set, allocates a 20-byte cleared block, initializes it through unnamed routines and stores a result in a field. It returns the block, minus one when a step fails, and zero when the flag is clear.

name: stub_return_minus_one
description: Returns the value minus one without doing any other work.

name: build_entry_chain
description: Builds a chain of entries by repeatedly allocating a 16-byte cleared block, attaching it through an unnamed routine, and filling a sub-block sized from a byte field. It returns the first entry, minus one when any step fails, and zero when the request count is zero.

name: link_entry_chain_pass
description: Walks through entries, allocating and linking nested items through unnamed routines. It returns the last linked entry, or minus one when a step fails.

name: create_and_add_library_base
description: Allocates a library base block through a library call and, when that succeeds, stores two values in it and registers it with the system library list. It returns minus one on success and zero if the allocation fails.

name: bump_counter_and_clear_bit
description: Increments a 16-bit counter in a library record and clears bit five of a status byte in the same record.

name: decrement_and_notify_when_idle

name: unlink_and_release_or_mark

name: unlink_and_release_entry

name: parse_translation_entry_text

name: return_low_word

name: terminate_string_return_word

name: scan_pattern_table_matches

name: process_escape_sequences_in_text

name: copy_escaped_text_segment

name: copy_text_segment_trimmed
description: Copies a counted run of text into a destination buffer, trimming trailing flagged characters. It sets a flag when the following character is a backtick.

name: copy_counted_text_run

name: trim_trailing_text_flags
description: Walks back from the end of a text buffer while characters are flagged in a table, then writes a zero terminator after the last kept character.
